extracted_information: The web content discusses using Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) for trace collection and analysis within .NET applications. It highlights the .NET TraceProcessing API as a primary tool for accessing ETW trace data using C#. While not explicitly stating 'real-time monitoring', the mention of 'streaming' in related topics implies capabilities for processing live trace data. The content recommends the `Microsoft.Windows.EventTracing.Processing.All` NuGet package and provides a direct link to GitHub samples for code examples.

features.name: ETW (Event Tracing for Windows)
features.description: Powerful trace collection system built-in to Windows OS. Provides structured events for automated data processing, unlike text logging. Offers deep integration with system behavior, including kernel-level events like context switches, memory allocation, process create/exit.

features.name: .NET TraceProcessing API
features.description: A .NET API created by Microsoft for accessing many kinds of ETW trace data. Used internally by Microsoft for automated trace analysis and within Windows Performance Analyzer (WPA). Allows analysis of applications and systems with the same tools Microsoft uses.

references.name: Windows Performance Analyzer (WPA)
references.description: Provides a graphical interface for visualizing and exploring ETW trace data (.etl files).
